commits.message:
threat model: docs/threat-model.md, and the documents that point at it

The installation's threat model gets its own page at the root of docs/:
the stance, who can act class by class, what is defended, and the test a
security finding must pass. It carries rfc-005 §3 to §6 as built: the
first half of the merge boundary as the partition made it, with the
re-issue of physical's earlier credentials as the condition it holds
under; the second half as unenforced today, with the clearance check the
operator ruled for and the residuals it leaves; the workstation's
accepted residual; and the pins by class, each class defined and its
instances named from the versions: block, with the pins that name a
version alone and the cluster's unaged images and charts as accepted
residuals.

architecture.md §4.1 becomes the cluster's controls and residuals under
the page, records the host-network residual of the metadata deny, and
accepts the controller-door residual for a dial over the server LAN
rather than naming a certificate pin as its retirement. The fence's
sentence in §4.3 and the dispatch App's register row say what the forge
enforces: a token with contents:write merges a green pull request that
changes no workflow file. The findings register reads its grades against
the page. The dispatch protocol gains the rule on forge text (§1) and
the rule on security findings (§3). README links the page, and rfc-005
moves to Implemented.

Closes Aetf/kluster-ops#496.

threat model: ci.md's dispatch-token residual and unifi.py's controller-door comment match what the forge and the model say

framework/ci.md §3 said the dispatch App's token pushes never to
kluster's main and called that the boundary anyone who can push a branch
already has; main requires checks and restricts nobody, so the token's
contents:write merges a green pull request that changes no workflow
file. The comment on ALLOW_INSECURE named a certificate pin as what
would retire the controller-door residual; architecture.md §4.1 accepts
it for a dial over the server LAN and leaves a dial over the cluster
VLAN uncovered. The page's residual for images a chart names by tag
points at Aetf/kluster-ops#503.
